title: How to use a nasal spray correctly
also: how to use a nose spray
what: How to use a nose spray so the medicine goes inside your nose and does not run down your throat.
why: When your doctor has prescribed a spray for a runny nose, allergy, sinusitis or other reasons.
duration: the procedure itself takes less than a minute
tell_doctor: If you have used a decongestant spray for a long time and cannot breathe without it
If you have high blood pressure or heart disease

prepare.title: Nose
prepare.text: Gently blow your nose before using the spray.

prepare.title: Bottle
prepare.text: A new bottle usually needs a few sprays into the air first - see the instructions.

prepare.title: Children
prepare.text: Children need a children's form and dose - ask the pediatrician.

steps: Shake the bottle, if the instructions say so
Put the tip into one nostril and press the other with a finger
Point the tip toward the ear on the same side, not toward the middle wall of the nose
Press and at the same time breathe in gently through your nose
Repeat for the other nostril and wipe the tip
feel: Sometimes mild stinging or a taste in the mouth
If it runs down your throat - you breathed in too hard or tipped your head back
after: Do not sniff hard right after the spray
Decongestant sprays are usually not used longer than a few days - ask your doctor
Do not share a bottle with other people
red_flags: A nosebleed that does not stop for 20 minutes - call your local emergency number
Swelling of the face or trouble breathing - call your local emergency number

faq.q: Why not spray toward the middle wall?
faq.a: That irritates the lining and can cause bleeding. Pointing toward the ear is safer.

faq.q: Can I get used to a spray?
faq.a: To decongestant ones, yes, if used for a long time. Tell your doctor if you cannot manage without it.

reminders.text: Time for your nose spray. Blow your nose, head slightly forward, tip toward the ear.
